years.source: [EUR] https://www.unilever.com/files/91ad891b-a5cd-4a79-823d-83b82b31615a/ir-q4-2022-full-announcement.pdf (Unilever Q4/FY2022 Full Year Results announcement, unaudited but matches audited Annual Report figures) | Consolidated income statement, balance sheet, cash flow statement, Unilever Q4 2022 Full Year Results (RNS announcement). Currency: EUR millions. Total Debt = Bank loans and overdrafts (519) + Bonds and other loans, carrying amount (26,512) = 27,031; EXCLUDES lease liabilities (1,408) for consistency with other companies. Interest Expense = gross "Finance costs" (818) before netting Finance income (281) and pension interest. Capex = "Net capital expenditure" (1,627) from FCF reconciliation -- this document does NOT separately disclose gross purchases of PPE vs intangibles vs disposal proceeds (unlike the FY2024 announcement which does), so this figure is net of disposal proceeds, NOT strictly comparable to gross capex used for other companies -- flag in ratio analysis. COGS (35,906) is NOT from Unilever's own disclosure (their trading statements go straight from Turnover to Operating profit with no Cost of Sales line) -- sourced from third-party financial data (Yahoo Finance/S&P Capital IQ standardized income statement) which matches Unilever's turnover exactly but reclassifies opex differently, so their own "Operating Income" figure doesn't match Unilever's reported 10,755 -- treat COGS/gross margin ratios for Unilever with more caution than other companies.

[EUR] https://www.unilever.com/files/ir-q4-2024-full-announcement.pdf (Unilever Q4/FY2024 Full Year Results announcement, showing FY2023 as prior-year comparative) | Consolidated income statement, balance sheet, cash flow statement, Unilever Q4 2024 Full Year Results (FY2023 comparative columns). Currency: EUR millions. Total Debt = Bank loans and overdrafts (506) + Bonds and other loans, carrying amount (26,692) = 27,198; excludes lease liabilities (1,395). Interest Expense = gross Finance costs (1,038). Capex = Net capital expenditure (1,703) per FCF reconciliation, net of disposal proceeds -- same limitation as FY2022. COGS (34,429) is third-party sourced (Yahoo Finance/S&P Capital IQ), not from Unilever's own abbreviated trading statement income statement -- same caveat as FY2022 applies.

[EUR] https://www.unilever.com/files/ir-q4-2024-full-announcement.pdf (Unilever Q4/FY2024 Full Year Results announcement) | Consolidated income statement, balance sheet, cash flow statement, Unilever Q4 2024 Full Year Results (RNS announcement). Currency: EUR millions. Total Debt = Bank loans and overdrafts (521) + Bonds and other loans, carrying amount (28,648) = 29,169; excludes lease liabilities (1,486). Interest Expense = gross Finance costs (1,113). Capex = GROSS this year: Purchase of intangible assets (233) + Purchase of property, plant and equipment (1,738) = 1,971 -- NOTE this is gross unlike FY2022/23 net figures used above, since this year's announcement separately disclosed the components; minor inconsistency across years flagged for transparency. COGS (33,391) is third-party sourced (Yahoo Finance/S&P Capital IQ) -- Unilever's own trading statement does not disclose a Cost of Sales line; treat gross margin/COGS-based ratios for Unilever with more caution than for the SEC-filing companies (Apple, Walmart, Microsoft, Enron) where COGS is directly as-reported.
